clue.text: Qualify to get drink producing ID

parts.note: to pass a test is to qualify
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Getting a drink after qualifying seems to produce identification, as if a pub demanded it.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the standard document travellers show as identification.

clue.text: Temporary retail outlets in post offices enthralling youngster

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the post offices word holds the youngster word

parts.note: PO is post office, POS its plural
a pup is a young animal

explanation.surface: Short-lived shops set up inside post offices delight a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop-ups are shops or stalls opened for a short time only.

clue.text: Inquirer ekes out sign of hesitation

indicators.note: out means put wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone asking questions eked out a hesitant 'er'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seeker is one who searches or looks for answers, as an inquirer does.

clue.text: Selects note in audition as fairy

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, so the letters are what is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: picks means selects; E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A fairy selects a note during an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: PICKS plus E, said out, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pixie is a small mischievous sprite of folklore, a kind of fairy.

clue.text: Remains in lodge outside university

indicators.note: outside says the lodge word goes round the university letter

parts.note: to lodge somewhere is to reside there

explanation.surface: Someone stays on at a lodge just outside the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over, the remains.

clue.text: Black king you're initially finding dull

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as in pencil grades
Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A chess player finds the black king rather dull to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dim and blurred, so bleary works as a synonym for dull in that sense.

clue.text: Reprobate tribe disbanded during occupation

indicators.note: during says the scattered letters sit within the occupation word

parts.note: one's line is one's line of work, an occupation

indicators.note: disbanded means broken up, so the letters of tribe are scattered

explanation.surface: A tribe was broken up while their land was under military occupation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disbanded' signals the anagram and 'during' the insertion; 'occupation' means line of work here, not a military one.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine is a dissolute, immoral person, which is what a reprobate is.

clue.text: Article and note supporting main upset for art lover

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts these pieces below the reversed main word
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the main word reads bottom to top

parts.note: the main is the open sea
the is the definite article
te is a note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: An article and note backing a mainstream upset, written for a lover of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SEA into AES; 'supporting' puts THE and TE beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is someone with a refined appreciation of beauty and the arts.

clue.text: American convict in square with chick

parts.note: a yard is an enclosed square of ground, a courtyard
bird is slang for a young woman, as is chick

explanation.surface: A US prisoner shares the exercise square with a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardbird is American slang for a prisoner, someone confined to the prison yard.

clue.text: Expert is broadcast live before now

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of these two words are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: An expert is on a broadcast that goes out live, ahead of now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges EXPERTIS; 'live' looks like a broadcasting word but is a verb in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To preexist is to exist, that is to be alive or present, at an earlier time.

clue.text: One taking advantage of a vehicle ferry regularly

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of ferry, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone exploits a vehicle ferry service that runs on a regular timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ER from the even letters of ferry.
explanation.definitionFit: An abuser exploits or mistreats something, taking unfair advantage of it.

clue.text: Set foot in gastro diner

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the letters of gastro diner

explanation.surface: Someone steps into a gastropub-style diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Trod is the past tense of tread, which means stepped or set foot.

clue.text: Candidate in sandwich shop having goal to meet the Queen

parts.note: Pret A Manger is a British chain of sandwich shops, often just called Pret
an end is an aim or goal
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: An election candidate holds a meeting with the Queen in a sandwich shop.
explanation.walkthrough: PRET is the British sandwich chain Pret A Manger.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is a claimant to a throne or title, so a candidate for it.

clue.text: Treatment facility in pub holding male back

indicators.note: back says the combined letters are read in reverse
holding says the pub word wraps around the male word

parts.note: a bar is a pub
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A treatment centre operates inside a pub that is keeping a man back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal, applied after 'holding' puts the man inside the pub, not a body part or a place behind the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is short for a rehabilitation clinic where addicts are treated.

clue.text: Confront exterior features

definitions.meaning: the front surface of the head bearing the eyes, nose and mouth; also the outer surface of a building

explanation.surface: Confront exterior features.
explanation.definitionFit: Face as a verb means to stand up to; as a noun it is a visible front surface.

clue.text: Designer in the Arctic collapsed

indicators.note: collapsed means fallen to pieces, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A designer was caught up when the Arctic ice collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect designs buildings, and by extension anything planned.

clue.text: Vagrant putting newspaper in towel?

indicators.note: putting with in says the newspaper is placed within the towel word
in, paired with putting, says the newspaper letters go inside the towel word

parts.note: a towel dries you, so it is a drier, hence the question mark
FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A tramp wraps a newspaper inside a towel to keep warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a towel is a drier only loosely; 'putting ... in' places FT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter wanders from place to place without settled home or work, like a vagrant.

clue.text: Gatecrashes popular, authentic society holding first of dances

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: holding says these pieces wrap around the dance letter

parts.note: true means genuine, authentic

indicators.note: first of says to take the opening letter of dances

explanation.surface: A popular, genuine society is hosting dances, which uninvited people crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' sets D (first of dances) inside TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to enter uninvited, which is what gatecrashers do.

clue.text: Funny person I scold about clothing

parts.note: a card is a joker or amusing character

indicators.note: about says the scold word is turned round

parts.note: to nag is to scold

explanation.surface: A joker admits to scolding someone about what they're wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted jacket, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Sister almost trips avoiding duke in shades

indicators.note: almost says to drop the last letter of the sister word

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

indicators.note: avoiding says the duke's letter is left out of the dance word

parts.note: to trip is to dance lightly, so trips are dances

explanation.surface: A nun nearly stumbles while dodging a duke, all while wearing sunglasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts NUN to NU; 'avoiding' takes D from DANCES to leave ANCES. 'trips' as dances is the literary 'trip the light fantastic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuances are subtle gradations of meaning or colour, which are shades.

clue.text: Soloist not even opening

indicators.note: not even says to keep the odd-numbered letters of soloist and drop the even ones

explanation.surface: A soloist isn't even opening the concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A slit is a narrow cut or opening.

clue.text: Way to record pace

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A method for recording one's walking speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single pace in walking.

clue.text: Presume dancing is best

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of presume are rearranged

explanation.surface: Assume that dancing is the best thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in quality, the very best.

clue.text: John or Paul perhaps got the best of the French

parts.note: beat means defeated, got the best of
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Two apostles, perhaps, outdid the French.
explanation.walkthrough: John and Paul look like apostles or popes; they are John Lennon and Paul McCartney.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lennon and Paul McCartney were members of the Beatles, so each is a Beatle.

clue.text: High Street I deserted

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: I deserted the High Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks part of 'High Street' but is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned is slang for intoxicated by drugs, which is to be high.

clue.text: Artist finally sculpted two bones

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: finally says to take the closing letter of sculpted

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An artist has at last sculpted two bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone; radii is its plural, so a pair of such bones.

clue.text: Carry out utensil

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan is to carry it out

explanation.surface: Carry out utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: Implement as a verb is to put into effect; as a noun it is a working tool.

clue.text: Raptor starts to eat allosaurus, gauging left eyeball

indicators.note: starts to says to take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A bird of prey begins to eat a dinosaur, eyeing up the left eyeball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raptor' suggests a dinosaur, as in Velociraptor, beside the allosaurus; here it is a bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey, which is what a raptor is.

clue.text: Measure jade green boxes

indicators.note: boxes means contains, so the answer sits inside the run of letters in jade green

explanation.surface: A unit of jade green paint comes in boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A degree is a unit of measure, of angle or temperature.

clue.text: Female embracing crew in lift

indicators.note: embracing says the female word wraps around the crew word

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A woman hugs a crew member in the lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten something is to raise or intensify it, which is to lift it.

clue.text: Special educational needs bothered governing body

parts.note: SEN is the British abbreviation for special educational needs in schools
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means bothered

explanation.surface: A school's governing body is troubled by special educational needs provision.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN is the standard British school abbreviation for special educational needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative or governing council, as in a university or state.

clue.text: Clergyman trailing king is always close

indicators.note: trailing says the other pieces follow behind the king's letter

parts.note: R is short for Rex, king
ever means always
a close is an end

explanation.surface: A clergyman following a king is always nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is the noun (an end), not the adjective meaning near.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title used for, and colloquially a word for, a minister of the church.
